From: Alex Li <alex.li@fastcommerce.com>

Subject: Follow-up from demo — latency & throughput targets

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — it was helpful. As we discussed, we want to confirm our production targets so you can advise on hosted vs dedicated. Key points from our side: 

- Steady-state QPS: ~100 qps
- Peak/spike: bursts up to ~800 qps for short windows (minutes), expected maybe 2–3 times/day
- Typical prompt length: ~60 tokens; typical response length: ~90 tokens
- Target p95 latency for inference (generation): <= 150 ms (preferably <=120 ms)
- Models: planning to use an LLM comparable to an 8B dense model (open weights), quantized option acceptable
- Security: SOC 2 is required; no immediate data residency restriction, but we may need VPC later for PCI-sensitive flows

Attaching our traffic profile export and a short CSV of expected hourly load. Could you summarize what you’d recommend for deployment mode given these numbers and next steps for a pilot? Also include rough pricing at the baseline pilot level (3 months).

Cheers,
Alex

Thanks Alex — good notes and thanks for the CSV. Quick recap and proposed next steps below. I’m looping in Ben (solutions engineering) and Neha (sales) so we can align on a pilot plan and run an initial benchmark.

Recap of what I heard:
- Steady 100 qps, short spikes up to ~800 qps
- p95 target <=150 ms (goal <=120 ms)
- Model roughly 8B-equivalent, prompts ~60 tokens, responses ~90 tokens
- SOC 2 required; VPC possible later for PCI

Initial recommendation (short answer):
- Start with a hosted API pilot using reserved baseline capacity + burst routing for spikes. Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and lets us validate p95 under real traffic quickly.
- If after a controlled benchmark/2-week pilot we cannot reliably meet p95 <=150 ms with acceptable cost, move to Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) — we’ve found Dedicated provides tighter p95 consistency for these spike profiles.

What we need from you to size and run the pilot:
1) Confirm which model variant you plan to run (name or nearest public equivalent) and whether you’ll use quantized weights.
2) A short sample prompt set (5–10 representative prompts) and the CSV you already shared — thanks for that.
3) Any concurrency limits on your side (client-side QPS caps, retry/backoff behavior).

Planned next steps on our side:
- Ben will spin up a hosted benchmark harness (we’ll use your traffic CSV + your sample prompts) and run a few load profiles.
- Deliverables: benchmark report (p50/p95/p99), cost estimate for hosted pilot, and a Dedicated sizing sketch (if needed).
- I’ll share a pilot pricing estimate and an SLA tiers PDF so you can see tradeoffs.

If you’re comfortable, we’ll start the hosted benchmark this week. Otherwise we can schedule a short 30-min call for alignment.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Irene — thanks, that plan looks good. A few clarifications to help size the benchmark: 

- Model: we plan to start with an open 8B-context model (approx equivalent to meta-8B dense). We'll test with 8-bit quantized weights in staging.
- Prompts: I’ll drop 8 representative prompts into the Drive folder (short product search flows + cart summaries).
- Client behavior: our frontend applies linear backoff after two retries; concurrency per worker is limited to 16 connections but we have ~30 workers across regions.
- Security: SOC 2 is necessary; VPC will be a later conversation (probably before production).

We’re happy to start the hosted benchmark. One thing: cost sensitivity is real — if hosted to meet p95 <=120 ms increases unit cost by more than ~2x vs our target, procurement will push for Dedicated. If you can include a cost delta forecast in the benchmark report that highlights when Dedicated becomes cost-advantageous, that would help.

Procurement contact: Samantha Park (samantha.park@fastcommerce.com).

Alex
